result.title: Gibbs Variational Last Layers for Long-Horizon Dynamics Learning
result.summary: Accurate long-horizon probabilistic predictions of dynamical systems are a prerequisite for model-based decision-making. Variational Bayesian last layers (VBLLs) are an attractive model class for this setting, offering tractable uncertainty at near-deterministic cost, yet they are trained exclusively with single-step likelihood objectives that may be insufficient for reliable multi-step rollouts. We revisit VBLLs through the lens of Gibbs variational inference, which decouples posterior inference from the choice of training loss. Building on this perspective, we introduce a family of multi-step training losses that progressively incorporate long-horizon structure, robustness via continuous ranked probability scores (CRPS), and training on full autoregressive rollouts. Our approach retains the simplicity of VBLLs while directly optimizing for multi-step predictive quality. Across illustrative synthetic environments, a diverse suite of chaotic dynamical systems, and real-world data, we show that multi-step, CRPS-based objectives substantially improve long-horizon accuracy and distributional fit, consistently outperforming single-step likelihood training.

AI.brief_summary: 该文从 Gibbs 变分推断视角重新审视变分贝叶斯末层（VBLL），提出一族多步训练损失，逐步引入长程结构、基于 CRPS 的分布拟合与全自回归 rollout 训练，以提升动力系统的长程概率预测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「解耦后验推断与训练损失」及多步 rollout 目标，可供核查 LVR 中轨迹训练、长程误差累积与逐步监督分配的问题，但任务域相距较远，属方法借鉴线索。
